description: Payments without borders should primarily be driven by reducing technical friction—through interoperability, standardization (e.g., ISO 20022), and seamless cross-border infrastructure—to enable faster, cheaper, and more inclusive global transactions. However, geopolitics will inevitably shape adoption and trust, as nations prioritize sovereignty, data control, and strategic interests in global payment ecosystems.

title: Building India's AI-Native Financial Infrastructure: Powering the Next Decade of Digital Public Infrastructure
track: AI Infrastructure, Digital Public Infrastructure, Agentic Finance
description: Artificial Intelligence is set to become the next foundational layer of India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), transforming how financial services are designed, delivered, and governed. This fireside chat will explore how AI-native infrastructure, accelerated computing, and intelligent financial systems can unlock new opportunities in payments, lending, fraud prevention, financial inclusion, and public service delivery. The discussion will examine the technologies, partnerships, and infrastructure required to build secure, scalable, and trusted AI-powered financial ecosystems for the next decade.

title: From Regulation to Transformation: Building India's Next-Generation Reform Architecture
track: Governance Reforms, Digital Public Infrastructure, Future-Ready Institutions
description: As India advances towards becoming a developed economy, the next wave of reforms must move beyond regulation towards creating agile, technology-enabled institutions that can anticipate change, foster innovation, and deliver better outcomes for citizens and businesses. This session will explore how governance, policy, digital public infrastructure, regulatory architecture, and institutional reforms can work together to build a future-ready state capable of supporting sustained economic growth. The discussion will examine how India can design next-generation reform frameworks that are collaborative, data-driven, globally competitive, and resilient, while maintaining trust, accountability, and ease of doing business in an increasingly digital and interconnected world.

This session will explore how industry, regulators, market infrastructure institutions, and open digital networks such as ONDC can collaborate to create the next generation of investment infrastructure that enhances accessibility, transparency, efficiency, and trust while powering Bharat's long-term wealth creation journey.

title: The Lending-Fintech Power Shift: As Lenders Build In-House Digital Lending Stacks, What's Left for Lending-Tech Platforms?

Discuss enabling a future-ready economy by supporting digital finance startups, enhancing infrastructure, and fostering public-private collaboration that creates a globally competitive ecosystem. Address leveraging Agentic AI, tokenisation, and quantum technologies to accelerate financial inclusion and align with GFF2026's vision of connected, inclusive financial systems driving Maharashtra toward becoming India's first trillion-dollar sub-national economy.

title: Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation and Quantum — Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance
track: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Inclusive Finance
description: The inaugural session of GFF2026 will set the agenda for the next era of financial innovation, where Agentic AI, tokenisation and quantum technologies converge to reshape finance at population and global scale. It will highlight the need for responsible innovation, resilient infrastructure, global interoperability and strong governance to ensure that emerging technologies move from potential to real-world impact.
